_what: Which failure code (src/failure-codes.json) an error the platform made is, read once by src/failure.mjs failureOf for an error that carries no Trillion failure_code. Rows are tried in order and the first that holds wins: `flag` holds when the error's property of that name is true; `contains` holds when the error's message contains those words, in any case; `reply_status` holds when the owner that refused answered one of those HTTP statuses (an error carries it as `reply_status`). An error no row names is `unexpected`. Adding a platform failure is a row here.

rows._why: SQLite refuses every write once a Durable Object's pages run out (workerd: 'Exceeded the maximum database size'). The same request asked again at once on a fresh handle fails the same way; the owner frees derived space (src/full-store-recovery.mjs) and the sender sends it again after the wait.

rows.contains: We encountered an internal error. Please try again. (10001)
rows._why: Cloudflare R2 documents code 10001 as HTTP 500 InternalError and recommends retrying the request. Wait before retrying; a fresh Durable Object handle cannot repair a storage service error. Match its specific code, not generic internal-error wording.
The storage service timed out and reset the object. A fresh handle cannot repair that operation inside the same request; wait before retrying, even when the platform marks the reset retryable.

rows._why: A call through a handle made by the Worker before an update reached the Worker after it.

An owner's reply of 400, 404, 413 or 422 is its deliberate refusal of what was asked, in words it wrote for the caller ("A list needs a label"). It is the caller's to correct and send again, so an AI is told to read the reason and correct the request; it was told `unexpected`, fatal, with the remedy 'use the error reference to investigate', which made a fixable mistake look like a defect and was logged as one. 401, 402 and 403 are access and plan answers that carry their own payload, 409 is an unsettled attempt, 5xx is not a refusal, so none of them is here.

own_words._what: Words a platform error carries that are the platform's own (its database's error and code), read by src/failure.mjs platformSaid: an answer to the person or their AI never repeats them; a failure Trillion did not expect answers its reference and plain words instead (src/tools.mjs). `contains` holds when the message contains those words, in any case; `code` holds when the error's code property is exactly that.
